sides.text: A 12 V battery is connected across a 240 Ω resistor. What current flows?
C. 50 mA
A 10 Ω resistor carries 2 A. How much power does it dissipate?
A. 40 W
100 Ω, 220 Ω, and 330 Ω resistors are in series. What is the total resistance?

more.text: Series resistances add. 57 Ω would be the parallel value.

sides.text: Two 100 Ω resistors are in parallel. What is the total resistance?
C. 50 Ω

more.text: Equal resistors in parallel give half the value.

sides.text: A 9 V source feeds a 6 kΩ resistor in series with a 3 kΩ resistor. What is the voltage across the 3 kΩ resistor?
D. 3 V
A 5 V supply drives a red LED (Vf = 2 V) at 20 mA. Which series resistor is needed?
A 60 W bulb runs for 5 hours. How much energy does it use?
D. 0.3 kWh
Which unit measures capacitance?
A. Farad

more.text: The farad. Henries measure inductance and coulombs measure charge.

sides.text: A resistor's bands are brown, black, red, gold. What is its value?

more.text: Brown 1, black 0, red ×100 gives 1,000 Ω. Gold is ±5%.

sides.text: Which component passes current in only one direction?
D. Diode

more.text: A diode conducts forward and blocks in reverse.

sides.text: A 10:1 step-down transformer has 120 V in. What is the output?
A. 12 V

more.text: The voltage ratio equals the turns ratio, so 120 / 10 = 12 V.

sides.text: Which tool shows a signal's shape over time?
C. Oscilloscope

more.text: A multimeter gives numbers. A scope shows the waveform.

sides.text: To measure the current through a load, how should a multimeter be connected?
options: Across the supply with the load removed

sides.text: B. In series with the load

more.text: Current must flow through the meter, so it's connected in series.

sides.text: A 2,000 mAh battery powers a 100 mA device. About how long does it last?
B. About 20 hours

more.text: 2,000 mAh / 100 mA = 20 h (ideally).

sides.text: Why do power lines use very high voltage?
options: To reduce current and I²R loss
To make them safe to touch

sides.text: A. To reduce current and I²R loss

more.text: For the same power, higher voltage means lower current and much lower loss.

sides.text: A 5 V PWM signal has a 40% duty cycle. What is its average voltage?
B. 2 V

more.text: Average = 0.4 × 5 = 2 V.

sides.text: Which of these is a full computer running Linux?
C. Raspberry Pi

more.text: The Raspberry Pi runs Linux. The others are microcontrollers.

sides.text: A 5 V sensor output drives a 3.3 V microcontroller pin. What is the risk?
C. Damage to the input

more.text: Over-voltage can damage the input. Use a level shifter or divider.

sides.text: What is 1101 in binary as a decimal number?
An AND gate has inputs 1 and 0. What is the output?

more.text: AND is high only when both inputs are high.

sides.text: What is the wavelength of a 100 MHz radio signal?
B. 3 m
About how many megabytes per second does a 100 Mbit/s link move?
B. 12.5 MB/s

more.text: Divide by 8 bits per byte.

sides.text: Which radio method varies the carrier's frequency to carry the signal?
D. FM

more.text: FM varies frequency; AM varies amplitude.

sides.text: Four 1.5 V cells are connected in series. What is the voltage?
C. 6 V

more.text: Series voltages add: 4 × 1.5 = 6 V.

sides.text: A 100 µF capacitor is charged to 5 V. How much charge does it hold?
C. 500 µC
Which part is placed beside an MCU's power pin to supply quick current bursts?
D. A 0.1 µF decoupling capacitor

more.text: Decoupling capacitors supply fast current and filter noise.

sides.text: A button input reads random values when it isn't pressed. What is the fix?
options: Add a pull-up or pull-down resistor

sides.text: B. Add a pull-up or pull-down resistor

more.text: A floating input needs a defined level.

sides.text: Which component stores energy in a magnetic field?
B. Inductor

more.text: Inductors store energy in magnetic fields; capacitors in electric fields.

sides.text: A 12 V source feeds two series resistors, and the first drops 5 V. What does the second drop?
B. 7 V

more.text: Kirchhoff's voltage law: 12 − 5 = 7 V.

sides.text: A wire is connected across a battery's terminals. What happens?
D. Very high current and heating

more.text: That's a short circuit: only the source and wire limit the current.
